findings.title: Observing one project erases other projects’ poll state
findings.description:
`RunnerTenant` shares one observer across all projects, but these lines discard every entry outside the current project. Even an empty second project clears the first project’s polling timestamps, overdue flags, and standing faults. Consequently, runs are polled every tick instead of respecting `run_poll_interval_seconds`.

Scope observer state and cleanup per project. Add a regression covering alternating projects, including an empty project.

findings.title: Launches can start after the budget expires
findings.description:
The budget check occurs before `_launch`, which then commits a journal entry and opens log files before calling `Popen`. If that work crosses the deadline—or shutdown is requested meanwhile—the subprocess still starts, violating the documented budget contract.

Recheck immediately before spawning and explicitly reconcile any journaled-but-unlaunched entry. Test deadline expiry and stop requests during journal issuance.

findings.title: Unconfirmed launch faults disappear between polls
findings.description:
A failed launch poll stores its fault in `_faulted`, but the next tick takes `_still_overdue` without replaying that fault. Unlike the confirmed-run path, it reports no standing observation failure. `ProjectTick._close_recovered` therefore closes the escalation despite no successful observation.

Replay the cached fault until a later observation establishes recovery. Add a test using fresh `TickFaults` on consecutive ticks within the polling interval.
